data.description: Observed live this tick (2026-08-30, ~20:5xZ). Read-path WAL staleness under the macOS Docker bind mount is known (ticks missed the message that fired them); this is the WRITE-path twin, verified: 'node apps/chat/bin/chat.js dm human:forrest ...' on the host reported success as message id 161 — but GET /api/messages?conversation=7 never showed it, and the server later assigned ids 165+ in the same conversation. The host CLI wrote into a stale host-side WAL view of apps/chat/data/chat.db that the containerized server does not share; the write is silently invisible (and id 161 may resurface as an orphan/duplicate after a checkpoint — check for it during fix verification). Impact: any host-side CLI write (dm, post, read) can silently fork the DB — worse than the read bug because it loses outbound board communication. Workaround used this tick and until fixed: all writes via the server HTTP API (POST /api/messages, /api/read, /api/dms). Fix direction for the planner (not binding): make bin/chat.js talk to the server API when the server is up (it is the single writer), or refuse to touch the DB file directly when a server lock/container is detected — silent success is the failure mode to remove.
data.title: chat CLI on host writes to a DB view the container server never sees — route CLI writes through the server API or fail loudly

data.body: Plan written. Decision: hybrid (a)+(b) — CLI auto-routes reads AND writes through the server HTTP API whenever a server is reachable; direct-DB mode survives only with an explicit alternate CHAT_DB or a positive connection-refused probe; any ambiguous probe (timeout, wrong shape, 5xx) refuses loudly and touches nothing. Invariant for QA: in API mode chat.js never opens a DB file. Six API parity gaps found and scoped into this task: /api/channels missing visibility+members (AS-22 was CLI-only), no /api/catchup, no forced-ingest /api/sync (server ingest is 10s-throttled vs CLI inbox's ingest-now contract), /api/messages missing limit, /api/roster requires me where CLI does not, no /api/dump or /api/export (stale export = wrong records commits; dump is the only private-channel backup). AS-7 sentinel unaffected (store-level, server writes it in API mode). Compose cli service gains CHAT_API=http://server:8347. Divergence-regression test specified (write via CLI must appear in the server's own GET /api/messages view — the exact check that caught orphan 161 — plus proof the CLI created no DB file).

Implementation complete on feat/AS-24-cli-write-safety (dab1202, e4e637e, 2520748). Built per plan: (1) six server parity gaps closed — POST /api/channels honors visibility/members with the AS-22 rule moved into store.createChannel; POST /api/catchup; POST /api/sync (unthrottled ingest); GET /api/messages ?limit=; GET /api/roster me-optional; GET /api/dump + /api/export (operator endpoints, same trust domain as raw DB). (2) bin/chat.js resolves mode once per invocation before any store open — CHAT_MODE forces, CHAT_API probed, CHAT_DB-alone stays direct (test hermeticity), default probes 127.0.0.1:8347; probe up -> API mode via new lib/client.js (CLI never opens a DB file), hard ECONNREFUSED/ENOTFOUND -> direct, anything ambiguous -> exit 1 AS-24 refusal with zero side effects. (3) compose cli service gets CHAT_API=http://server:8347 (verified live: env present, probe 'up'). Tests: 126 pass in-container (was 112; +9 mode.test.js incl. the divergence regression + no-DB-file invariant + AS-7 sentinel server-side, +5 api.test.js parity). Boring choices, noted: no stderr mode diagnostic added at all (plan left it optional; --json never carries mode); API backend strips server-side refs and the CLI re-annotates from local .lattice so --json is byte-identical across modes; roster rows in API mode come wholly from the server minus the web-only 'self' field; private create-channel member count in API mode = unique requested set (equals inserted rows by construction); invalid CHAT_MODE is a loud usage error; export default --out still derives from CHAT_DB/default data dir in both modes.

Orphan-161 verification (read-only, live server left running per board-side ops boundary): server's own view now assigns id 161 to a DIFFERENT message — a system:lattice ingest ('AS-22: planned → in_progress') in #lattice-events (conv 3, createdAt 2026-08-30T20:31:03Z). The host CLI's forked DM write (conv 7, agent:cto-owen|human:forrest) is ABSENT from the server view; conv 7 ids run ...160,163,165,168,172,173 — the gap is real and the host write lost the rowid race, i.e. the outbound board DM is gone from the canonical store (it was re-sent via the API workaround during the bug tick). ids are PK, so a checkpoint cannot 'resurface' a second 161 as a row — the residual risk is a stale host-side -wal/-shm pair. Definitive check needs the single writer quiesced; exact commands for the orchestrator (I did NOT run the stop/restart): cd apps/chat && docker compose stop server; sqlite3 data/chat.db "PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE);"; sqlite3 data/chat.db "SELECT id,conversation_id,author_id,substr(body,1,60),created_at FROM messages WHERE id IN (161,162) OR (conversation_id=7 AND id BETWEEN 158 AND 166) ORDER BY id;"; then DOCKER_BUILDKIT=1 COMPOSE_DOCKER_CLI_BUILD=1 docker compose up -d --build. NOTE the --build is load-bearing at merge time regardless: the live server container runs the pre-AS-24 image (no /api/sync|catchup|dump|export), and the new CLI in API mode calls POST /api/sync on every inbox — ticks will get 'No such endpoint' 404s until the server image is rebuilt. QA focus: mode.test.js divergence regression + zero-side-effect refusals; --json shape parity across modes (refs stripped/re-annotated); AS-3 (reply/@-resolution never creates DM rows via API) and AS-6 (hidden-channel probe parity) held in API mode; hermeticity (CHAT_DB-alone never probes 8347).

QA review (cold, branch diff master...feat/AS-24-cli-write-safety at 8c1596b): PASS — 8/8 acceptance criteria met. Verdict: pass with one trivial inline fix; recommend done + merge, with the merge-time rebuild caveat below.

Per-criterion:
1. Live-server write visibility — PASS. mode.test.js divergence regression: dm/post/read via CLI in API mode land in the server's own GET /api/messages view (the exact observation that failed for msg 161); AS-7 sentinel written server-side.
2. API mode never opens a DB file — PASS. openStore exists only inside createDirectBackend (grepped bin/chat.js + lib/client.js); phantom-CHAT_DB parent-dir-absent assertion runs in the regression test AND at the end of the 14-command API sweep.
3. No silent fallback on ambiguity — PASS. Tests cover probe timeout (raw TCP trap) and squatted port (wrong-shape JSON); I additionally attacked the untested 5xx row myself (local HTTP server returning 500): exit 1, empty stdout, refusal names AS-24 + CHAT_MODE=direct, phantom DB parent never created. CHAT_MODE=api with down server exits 1; invalid CHAT_MODE is a usage error; CHAT_MODE=direct provably never contacts a poisoned CHAT_API (connection counter).
4. CHAT_DB-only hermeticity + suite — PASS. 126/126 in-container (docker compose run test), twice: before and after my inline fix. Rule-4 hermeticity test present.
5. Six parity gaps + --json byte parity — PASS. 5 new api.test.js tests (channels visibility/members with store-level 400 + name-still-free check, catchup, sync unthrottled, messages ?limit, dump/export byte-faithful); roster me-optional. Refs stripped server-side shapes re-annotated locally; exact-key assertions on dm/post/read --json; no mode field anywhere in --json (dev chose no stderr diagnostic at all — within plan). privateMemberCount parity verified against store.createChannel: actor must be in members, insert is over validated ids, so unique-requested-set == inserted-rows exactly.
6. Containerized CLI proxies — PASS by construction: compose cli service sets CHAT_API=http://server:8347; probe/fallback semantics fully tested. Live in-container verification is only possible after the image rebuild (see caveat).
7. Orphan-161 check — PASS. Recorded in marcus's comment: id 161 reassigned to a lattice ingest in the server view, forked DM absent, ids are PK so no row resurrection; residual is the stale host -wal/-shm pair, quiesce commands handed to orchestrator.
8. Docs — PASS. README backend-modes section + env table (CHAT_MODE/CHAT_API); advance.md §1 rewritten to the self-routing CLI with raw-API fallback. CLAUDE.md wording correctly left to metawork.

Dump-over-HTTP / AS-6 question (attacked explicitly): NOT a violation in the current trust domain. GET /api/dump does return #board content to any caller who can reach the socket — but the API has never authenticated identity: any localhost caller could already read #board via /api/messages?me=<member> (me is client-asserted on every endpoint). /api/dump therefore grants no capability any principal lacked; exposure is bounded by the 127.0.0.1:8347:8347 host-side port map (verified in compose.yaml) + the compose-project containers, i.e. the same operator who can read the DB file — exactly the plan's documented decision, and dump was already the sanctioned raw exception as the sole private-channel backup. Verified live (read-only): current server still runs the pre-AS-24 image, /api/dump|/api/export|/api/sync all 404 today. BACKLOG (not a blocker, filing separately): before any non-loopback deployment (DO), the whole unauthenticated API — dump/export first — needs an authn story; also note the accepted ECONNREFUSED-during-server-startup race inherent to the plan's 'positive down' rule.

Roster 400→200: web UI always passes ?me= (public/app.js:181); no other /api/roster consumers found; loosening is backward-compatible. PASS.

Inline fix (trivial, behavior-neutral, committed as qa-priya, 8c1596b): lib/client.js used a literal NUL byte as the viewCache key separator, which made git classify the source file as binary (no diff/blame/text-grep). Replaced with the \x00 escape — runtime-identical string; suite re-run in-container after the edit, 126/126.

MERGE-TIME OPS (load-bearing): the live server container predates AS-24 — the new CLI's API-mode inbox calls POST /api/sync and will exit 1 on 'No such endpoint' until the image is rebuilt. At merge: DOCKER_BUILDKIT=1 COMPOSE_DOCKER_CLI_BUILD=1 docker compose up -d --build (and optionally run marcus's quiesced wal_checkpoint inspection while the server is stopped).
